input.story: Landlord in Noida is refusing to return my 40000 deposit and when I went to ask, his son pushed me and threatened to beat me up if I come again. Should I go to the police? I also want my money.

output.masked_story: Landlord in Noida is refusing to return my 40000 deposit and when I went to ask, his son pushed me and threatened to beat me up if I come again. Should I go to the police? I also want my money.

case.summary: The user is demanding the return of a 40,000 INR security deposit from their landlord in Noida. When the user confronted the landlord, the landlord's son physically pushed and threatened the user with violence.
case.user_goal: Wants to know if they should report the landlord to the police and wants to recover the deposit money.

timeline.event: User asked for the return of the deposit, and the landlord's son pushed and threatened them.

evidence_missing: chat history or written communication demanding refund
cctv footage or witness details of the physical threat
risk_signals: physical assault / pushed by landlord's son
follow_up_questions: Do you have a registered rent agreement or rent receipts for the deposit payment?
When did you vacate the property, or when was the deposit due for refund?
Do you have any WhatsApp messages or call recordings of the landlord refusing the deposit or making threats?

flags.message: This involves police or possible criminal matters. Talk to a lawyer before you act or say anything.

notes: Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You have a clear financial claim to recover your security deposit of Rs 40,000 [KB:ica_s73]. However, because you were physically pushed and threatened with violence, your safety comes first and this has taken a criminal dimension. While deposit disputes can generally be resolved through written demand or civil court [KB:deposit_civil_route], physical threats require immediate legal protection. You currently lack written evidence of the incident and rent agreement details, which weakens your immediate position without formal legal help.

options.title: Consult a lawyer or Legal Aid immediately
options.what_to_do: Before taking further direct action against the landlord, speak with a legal professional or file a report regarding the physical threat and assault.
options.cost: Varies / Free via Legal Aid if eligible

options.title: Gather documentary evidence
options.what_to_do: Collect bank statements showing the deposit payment of Rs 40,000 and try to get written or message acknowledgement of the deposit amount.

options.title: Send a legal notice for deposit recovery
options.what_to_do: Have a lawyer issue a formal legal notice demanding the refund of Rs 40,000 [KB:ica_s73] while noting the unlawful conduct.

proof_tips: Obtain bank statements clearly highlighting the Rs 40,000 deposit transfer to the landlord.
Preserve any WhatsApp messages, texts, or call records where the landlord mentions the rent, deposit, or tenancy.
Check if there are any CCTV cameras near the place where the physical incident occurred or witnesses who saw it.
what_i_dont_know: Whether you have a written or registered rent agreement.
Whether you have reported the physical assault and threat to the local police.
Whether you have vacated the premises completely.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: There is a serious safety concern involving physical assault and threat of violence, which involves potential police/criminal action. You need professional legal guidance before confronting the landlord or filing complaints.
assessment.reply:
I am so sorry you had to go through this. I am an assistant, not a lawyer, but your safety is the most important thing right now. 

Because the landlord's son physically pushed and threatened you, this is not just a deposit dispute—it involves a serious criminal angle. You have a legal right to claim your Rs 40,000 security deposit back [KB:ica_s73, KB:deposit_civil_route], but because of the physical threat, you should speak to a lawyer or legal advice provider before taking any step alone.

If you qualify, you can get free legal assistance through the District Legal Services Authority or call the NALSA helpline at 15100 [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid]. A lawyer can guide you on reporting the assault to the police safely while also sending a legal notice to recover your money.

Do you have a written rent agreement or any bank receipts showing the Rs 40,000 payment?
